transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-11-18
Time: 10:00 AM PST
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Sven Rasmussen (Redwood SE); Dr. Lena Ortiz (Novus Head of AI); Samir Patel (Novus Eng Mgmt); Olivia Reed (Novus Compliance)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
Weekly check-in focusing on quality evaluation and regression checks. Found a regression in the discharge-summary prompt set for oncology patients; false-positive hallucination about meds. Agreed to tune prompts, add stricter guardrails, run broader 10k sample, and share security docs.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we'll kick off, um, quick agenda — quality results, any regressions, tuning notes, next steps.
[00:08] Dr. Lena Ortiz: hi Maya, thanks. quick high level we ran the three prompt sets against the last snapshot, and um the discharge summaries were fine overall but we saw a bump in hallucinations specifically around med contraindications, which is a big no for us.
[00:20] Samir Patel: yeah like, for 2% of samples the model asserted a med that wasn't in the record, it sounded pretty confident which is the problem.
[00:28] Sven Rasmussen: ok thanks for that. quick clarification — which model variant are you evaluating on? the one we gave, redwood-v2-opt-8q?
[00:35] Dr. Lena Ortiz: correct, v2-opt-8q, 16k context. we also tried a non-quantized baseline from another provider and that one had similar — hm — actually slightly fewer med hallucinations but worse on instruction-following.
[00:48] Maya Chen: noted, so tradeoff there. can you share the failing examples? we uploaded a spreadsheet with the flagged examples into the shared drive link, uh, link: drive.google.com/novus-poc/eval-20261118 (see sheet 'failures')
[01:00] Samir Patel: yes sent, you can see rows 12-28 are problematic, there's some truncation too where the KV cache maybe didn't persist across turns, not sure.
[01:10] Sven Rasmussen: hmm truncation could be prefix handling — are you concatenating the entire chart or using the summary extractor?
[01:16] Samir Patel: we used the chart-concat approach, maybe we should try the extractor.
[01:20] Sven Rasmussen: yeah extractor helps reduce spurious context. also we recommend prefix mask to avoid angling the model into inventing specifics.
[01:27] Olivia Reed: from compliance, main concern is PHI leakage and that the model doesn't invent meds; we need guardrails and SSO/KMS setup. also SOC2 docs please.
[01:36] Maya Chen: absolutely, we'll share SOC2 and the security pack. Sven, can you go over the guardrails we propose?
[01:42] Sven Rasmussen: sure. high-level: 1) explicit negative examples in prompt ("do not invent meds; if unknown, say 'unknown'") 2) scoring threshold: any answer with hallucination score >0.3 gets redacted/flagged 3) regex-based postprocessing for meds & dosages — we have templates, will share. 4) use of KMS-wrapped keys in Private deployments if you go that route.
[02:05] Dr. Lena Ortiz: for the scoring threshold, is that something in Redwood console or do we run locally?
[02:10] Sven Rasmussen: we can provide the scoring script — it runs locally or as a Redwood eval job. if you want realtime blocking we'll need to wire up the route with a small policy check (latency impact minimal but exists).
[02:22] Samir Patel: latency is a concern — what's the per-request overhead on the policy check?
[02:26] Sven Rasmussen: about 30-50ms for a lightweight scoring pass, plus your usual model latency. if you move to Dedicated infra we can push that down further.
[02:35] Maya Chen: to be explicit on options: hosted API gets you fastest setup; dedicated reserved capacity improves tail latency and throughput; private/VPC gives you KMS and stronger controls. what's your priority now — latency or security?
[02:47] Dr. Lena Ortiz: security and correctness are top; latency is secondary but still important.
[02:52] Olivia Reed: also encryption at rest + audit logs — we need retention policy for logs, and the ability to redact transcripts.
[02:58] Maya Chen: yes we'll include audit log config and retention options in the pack.
[03:03] Samir Patel: back to the regression — you mentioned a change between last week's snapshot and this one, did we change prompt wording?
[03:08] Dr. Lena Ortiz: we did tweak the prompt to be more concise, I think that might have pushed the model to be more assertive.
[03:13] Sven Rasmussen: ok so step one: revert to prior prompt A and run the 1k test to see if regression disappears; step two: try the extractor approach; step three: add explicit negative instruction.
[03:23] Maya Chen: agreed. we'll push an updated prompt bundle to the shared drive along with the scoring script. Sven will also add the regex templates.
[03:30] Olivia Reed: and from legal/compliance we'll review the SOC2 and any KMS contract language.
[03:36] Maya Chen: timeline recap — Sven uploads prompts and scripts by tomorrow 2026-11-19, Maya will send security pack by 2026-11-20, Novus runs 10k sample and returns results by 2026-11-27, action items owners listed in the doc.
[03:49] Dr. Lena Ortiz: sounds good. one more question — you mentioned automated fallback to a safer model variant. could that be used for high-risk cases?
[03:58] Sven Rasmussen: yep we can route by policy. for high-risk routes we can force a lower-temperature variant or a specialized hallucination-safe model, and fall back to human review if confidence is low.
[04:08] Samir Patel: nice. what about cost impact? lower-temp or specialized model tends to be slightly higher cost, right?
[04:13] Maya Chen: depends on model size and quantization — we'll include cost delta estimates in the pricing doc.
[04:18] Olivia Reed: ok please include that, we need to build into the procurement case.
[04:22] Maya Chen: any other questions?
[04:25] Dr. Lena Ortiz: not from me. thanks everyone.
[04:27] Maya Chen: great thanks, we'll follow up with the docs and schedule the perf benchmark.
[04:31] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional speaker label mixups and minor transcription errors (e.g., 'KV cache' -> 'K V cash', 'quantized' -> 'con-tilized').
